rounds.text: Raj Oil Mills Ltd trades at an attractive P/E multiple of 14.7 [E1], which sits below the broader sector benchmark of 18.84x [E6]. This earnings discount is particularly compelling given that the company generates a return on assets of 10.97%, heavily outperforming the sector benchmark of 3.52% [E8]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded by two percentage points to 5% in March 2026 compared to three years prior [E23], demonstrating structural fundamental improvement. Long-term tracking reveals that five-year profit growth of 3% has outpaced a price decline of 5%, generating a fundamentals-led signal that the stock is potentially undervalued [E47]. The current market price requires only a modest 3.0% earnings growth to be justified according to reverse DCF modelling, aligning exactly with the base case assumption [E38]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is elevated at 62.22x on filed statements and 13.28x against sector peers [E2, E7], and a discounted cash flow model leaves a negligible margin of safety of -1.0% [E36, E37].

The valuation of Raj Oil Mills Ltd presents a significant disconnect between the company's underlying assets and its market price, evidenced by a staggering price-to-book ratio of 62.22x [E2]. This premium is further highlighted by a sector comparison where the company’s P/B of 13.28x vastly exceeds the sector benchmark of 1.83x [E7]. Investors are currently paying for this optimism without the benefit of a dividend yield, which stands at 0.00% [E4]. Furthermore, the company’s operational efficiency is showing signs of strain, as the quarterly operating margin has contracted by 4 percentage points compared to the year-ago quarter [E24]. A discounted cash flow analysis confirms that the current market price of ₹ 44.8 exceeds the calculated intrinsic value of ₹ 44, resulting in a negative margin of safety [E36, E37]. Conceded: the company maintains a P/E ratio below the sector benchmark [E6] and has demonstrated an improvement in operating margins over a three-year period [E23]. Despite these points, the valuation remains exposed to a clear blind-spot where excessive optimism is already priced into the stock [E63].
